newsitem.title: USA: Dole opens up narrow lead in Texas - poll.
newsitem.headline: Dole opens up narrow lead in Texas - poll.

text.p: Republican candidate Bob Dole has opened up a narrow lead over President Bill Clinton in Texas, according to an opinion poll published on Friday.
The poll showed Dole with 47 percent support and Clinton trailing with 42 percent in the Lone Star state.
Dallas billionaire Ross Perot scored five percent, and the remaining six percent of the 1,048 people interviewed Oct. 26-30 said they were still undecided.
Conducted by Blum & Weprin Associates Inc., the poll was commissioned by The Dallas Morning News and the Houston Chronicle and had a margin of error of 3.5 percentage points.

Recent polls had showed Clinton and Dole in a statistical tie and Republican Party officials, acknowledging that Texas was a must-win state for them, said the new numbers showed a clear advantage in the final days of the campaign.
Clinton has pushed aggressively to become the first Democratic presidential candidate to win Texas since 1976, and is to visit the state again this weekend.

Friday's poll showed that more Texans thought Clinton was bettter able to handle the issues of jobs and the economy than Dole, and only 26 percent of respondents said they thought Dole could meet his promise of cutting income taxes by 15 percent and balance the budget at the same time.
But 32 percent of those polled said honesty and integrity were the most important issues for them, while only 27 percent said the candidates' positions on other issues were the most important.
With character a key issue, Clinton scored a 27 percent approval rating while Dole's was 61 percent.
